replies.body:
@trask Thanks for flagging. 

Documented the rationale in the PR's Prototype section (per the new template):
 This PR is a doc-consistency fix for #92 the normative `mcp.server`  table omitted two attributes that the same doc's examples already showed on server spans, and that `mcp.client` already defines as opt-in. It is not introducing a new attribute.
 
No reference scenario currently emits `mcp.server` spans. All 27 scenarios under `reference/scenarios/` are client-side AI frameworks  that consume MCP servers, not implement them. The pre-existing normative `mcp.server` attributes (client.address, client.port, common MCP attrs) have no scenario coverage today either, so this PR  isn't introducing a new gap.
 
 Per `evaluate-reference.instructions.md`, recommending `leave unchanged; honest capture gap` here. A dedicated `reference/scenarios/mcp-server/` would credibly demonstrate these attributes from the Python MCP SDK's `tools/call` handler boundary, but that's a separate, meaningfully larger PR.

replies.body: what do you mean by closer? attributes in the table are sorted based on name and requirement level and this table is auto-generated

> what do you mean by closer? attributes in the table are sorted based on name and requirement level and this table is auto-generated

As @lmolkova mentioned, this table is auto-generated by weaver, attribute ordering is determined by name and requirement level. This PR only adds the missing attribute refs in `model/mcp/spans.yaml`, the rendered table layout isn't manually controlled.
